title: Occupancy and Residency Certification: Transfer Window by Sender of a Turned-Away Notice
content:
The **transfer window** is a number of calendar days used under the Occupancy and Residency Certification product in fixing the start date of a borrower's health-care absence. It depends on who sent the turned-away notice — the rejected health-care absence notice about the monitored borrower received most recently — compared with the co-borrower named on the monitored Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM) loan record:

| Sender of the turned-away notice | Transfer window |
|---|---|
| the co-borrower named on the monitored HECM loan | 30 days |
| anyone else | 10 days |
| no turned-away notice on file | zero days |

## Points of judgement

- The comparison is with the co-borrower the HECM loan record names, not with any relative of the borrower.
- Where the profile monitors no HECM loan, no co-borrower is named, so a turned-away notice from any sender gives 10 days.
- *Hypothetical case.* A turned-away notice sent by the borrower's adult child, who is not the co-borrower named on the HECM loan, gives a transfer window of 10 days.
